title: Epochal attention kernel autotuner & phase-gated scheduler
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: In multi-GPU inference runs we observe variable tail latency and suboptimal throughput when attention kernels are selected independently per-device and when attention fusion windows slip relative to cross-device communication phases. This ticket proposes an "epochal" autotuner that (1) profiles short-run sequence-length and batch-shape distributions per-device, (2) derives a phase-gated schedule that aligns attention-kernel fusion windows with collective communication windows, and (3) exposes a light-weight runtime crediting mechanism to equalize latency spikes across devices.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype autotuner that runs a 1s profile and emits per-device kernel hints integrated into the runtime policy
Phase-gated scheduler that can shift microwindows by up to 3ms to align with communication without violating latency SLOs
End-to-end bench: >=10% throughput improvement or >=10ms 95th latency reduction on at least two internal multi-GPU workloads (8x A100 and 4x A40) vs baseline
No more than 3% increase in CPU usage on the host, and no memory growth in the runtime KV cache beyond current headroom
Canary rollout plan and rollback hooks documented in the PRD and release notes
implementation_notes: Autotuner: run micro-probes at request admission to collect seq-len histogram, attention sparsity hints and KV cache reuse stats. Keep profiling window <=1s to limit overhead.
Kernel hint format: compact token (kernel_id, fusion_hint, preferred_block_sz) pushed to conductor; allow soft fallbacks.
Phase gating: introduce a lightweight epoch counter per-worker and allow microwindow offsets (quantized at 0.5ms) controlled by conductor policy.
Credits: leaky-bucket credits per-device to delay non-critical prefills by small amounts when imbalance detected; credits replenished based on observed throughput.
Telemetry: add new measures: epoch_alignment_gap_ms, kernel_mismatch_rate, credit_backlog, per-device_seq_histogram to runtime telemetry sampling payloads.
Compatibility: must interoperate with Dedicated and Private deployments; kernel hints are a local optimization and must be safe to drop when heterogeneous device capabilities differ.
Fallback: if collective comm overlap is poor, fall back to conservative kernel selection (lower fusion, smaller blocks) to preserve 99th percentile latency.
Docs & UX: Console should show per-route "epoch alignment" and suggested autotuner settings; include an opt-out flag at route-level for customers who want deterministic behavior.
comments: 2026-02-15 Aisha K: Initial triage - this grows out of customer reports about long tail spikes on multi-GPU shards and internal noise during large-batch A/B tests. Spike planned to validate probing cost.

2026-02-20 Mateo A: Spike complete - microbench harness (8xA100) shows autotune probes add ~0.8% CPU and reduce kernel mismatch rate from 14% -> 4% for common workloads. Raw token throughput improved 12% for std-batched chat workload.

2026-02-24 Paulo R (perf): Observed a pathological workload with alternating short/long sequences where aggressive phase shifts increase 99th latency. Added credit leaky-bucket idea to smooth bursts; will add unit tests for bursting behavior.

2026-02-26 Design review notes: UX wants a visibility panel for epoch alignment and a control slider for aggressiveness (conservative | balanced | aggressive). PM requests default to 'balanced' for public API, conservative for Private by default.

2026-02-28 Mateo A: First integration PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2379. Hooks added to conductor, small protobuf schema change for kernel hints. Running CI + perf regressions.

2026-03-01 Infra: Canary infra requires minor config change to dedicated autoscaler to allow microwindow offsets; created infra ticket INF-1198 and added to dependencies. Blocking on dedicated canary permission for next rollout.

Notes/Tradeoffs: More aggressive phase gating yields better throughput but increases risk of misalignment on heterogeneous clouds. We prioritize conservative fallbacks and runtime guardrails to avoid customer-facing regressions.
